title: Danaher to Launch First AI Autonomous Lab to Speed Discovery 8x
summary:
A new research center at Abcam will leverage robotics and artificial intelligence to scale the generation of affinity reagents from tens to hundreds per year. The facility will combine technology from Danaher subsidiaries, including Cytiva and Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, with automation from startup Automata to establish a continuous 'design-make-test-learn' loop. This first autonomous lab for the company is designed to discover antibodies and reagents up to 8x faster than current methods and will scale operations in early 2027.

Shares of Danaher rose 1.3% in premarket trading after the announcement. The company plans to use the laboratory as a proof point for how its agentic systems and AI-ready data can accelerate medical progress, noting that the robotic approach will complement traditional immunization-based discovery methods.

selectedTweets.text:
Danaher $DHR is combining technology from several of its bioprocessing and life science companies with  Lab Robotics startup Automata to launch an AI-powered robotic autonomous research lab. 

From the Press Release: 

Danaher's first AI-powered autonomous lab is designed to deliver:
- Speed: Up to 8x faster discovery of affinity reagents, helping researchers get from idea to breakthrough sooner
- Scale: Unlocking up to a tenfold increase in annual reagent generation, from tens to hundreds of reagents per year as the lab scales
- Quality: Each design built in the lab would also be verified, tested and fed back to improve the next, without trading speed for scientific rigor
- Sustainability: Over time, this approach is expected to complement traditional immunization-based methods used in the discovery of antibodies and other research tools

Based at Abcam, a Danaher company, the lab uses AI to help create new affinity reagents, including antibodies, then builds and tests each one, feeding every result back into the model to improve the next design. The lab brings together industry-leading technologies and expertise from several Danaher operating companies, including Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, Cytiva, Genedata, Integrated DNA Technologies, and Molecular Devices, in one connected workflow. The device orchestration and robotic automation is the result of collaborative work with Automata*. 

This continuous design-make-test-learn loop can run in a fraction of the time it takes today, without trading speed for scientific rigor. This approach applies the same test-and-verify discipline of continuous improvement long used across Danaher operations to an AI-enabled laboratory environment. The lab is set to be an early proof point for how Danaher's smart instruments, AI-ready data, and expert agentic systems can accelerate scientific discovery and medical progress.
